issues.t: Head gasket failure and overheating (Northstar head bolts)
issues.sym: The temperature gauge climbs or an Engine Hot message appears, coolant keeps going down, white smoke comes from the exhaust, or the coolant tank bubbles.
issues.why: On the Northstar V8 the head bolt threads in the aluminum block can pull out or the bolts can loosen, so the head gaskets start leaking. GM issued a revised head bolt tightening spec and ran a campaign for loose head bolts on some cars. Owners report coolant loss and overheating, often past 80,000 miles.
issues.next: Stop driving if the engine overheats. Ask for a cooling system pressure test and a combustion gas test. A lasting fix usually needs thread inserts in the block, so get a quote from a shop that knows Northstars and compare it with what the car is worth.

issues.t: Engine burns oil
issues.sym: You need to add a quart of oil every 500-1,000 miles, the low oil warning comes on, or there is a puff of blue smoke at startup.
issues.why: Northstar engines of this era often use a lot of oil because carbon sticks the piston rings. GM issued several bulletins on higher than expected oil use and on knocking with oil use for the 4.6L engines.
issues.next: Check the oil at every fill-up and never let it run low. A shop can try a ring cleaning service first. Heavy oil use that keeps getting worse usually means internal engine work.

issues.t: Oil leaks from the lower crankcase and oil pan seal
issues.sym: Oil spots under the car, a burning oil smell after driving, or oil wet on the bottom of the engine.
issues.why: The joint between the upper and lower halves of the Northstar block and the oil pan seal commonly seep with age. GM later released improved sealing procedures for the crankcase, oil plate and oil pan.
issues.next: Have the source of the leak confirmed. The proper repair often means lowering the engine cradle, so it costs a lot in labor. Small seeps can be watched as long as you keep the oil topped up.

issues.t: Coolant leaks from the water pump or thermostat housing
issues.sym: Coolant level dropping, a sweet smell, drips under the front of the engine, a whining noise from the water pump, or a low coolant warning.
issues.why: GM bulletins cover coolant and oil leaks on 4.6L engines and a loose thermostat at the water pump cover, a bulletin that runs through the 2003 Eldorado. Owners also report water pump leaks and noisy pump bearings.
issues.next: Top up with the correct coolant and get the leak found soon. Running a Northstar low on coolant can overheat it and ruin the head gaskets.

issues.t: No-start from the PASS-Key anti-theft system
issues.sym: The engine will not crank or will not start, and the security light flashes. It can come and go.
issues.why: The Eldorado uses a key with a resistor pellet (PASS-Key). Worn key pellets, broken wiring in the ignition cylinder and failing modules make the car think the wrong key is in use. RepairPal lists this as the most common Eldorado problem.
issues.next: Try your spare key. If the security light stays on, leave the key in the on position for about 10 minutes and try again. Have a shop test the key and the wiring in the steering column.

issues.t: Instrument cluster short can cause no-start (recall)
issues.sym: The gauges and warning lights go blank or flicker, and the car may not start.
issues.why: An internal short in the analog instrument cluster can disrupt the PASS-Key anti-theft system and the gauges. Some owners reported trouble even on cars outside the recall VIN range.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 95V-224 at nhtsa.gov or with a Cadillac dealer and have the free repair done if it is still open.

issues.t: Fuel rail tubing can crack and leak (recall)
issues.sym: A raw gas smell under the hood or fuel wetness on top of the engine.
issues.why: The nylon tubing in the fuel rail can crack with age and heat and leak fuel into the engine bay, which is a fire risk. GM replaced the rail with a stainless steel one and a revised return line.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 04V-110 at nhtsa.gov or with a Cadillac dealer. If you smell fuel, do not drive the car; have it towed.

issues.t: ABS can cycle during normal braking (recall)
issues.sym: The brake pedal pulses and the ABS kicks in during an ordinary stop, which makes the car take longer to stop.
issues.why: The electronic brake control module (or the combined brake and traction module) could trigger the antilock brakes when they were not needed.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 97V-064 at nhtsa.gov or with a Cadillac dealer and have the free module replacement done if it is still open.

issues.t: Evaporative purge wiring routed wrong (recall)
issues.sym: Usually nothing you would notice; in some cars the wiring can rub and cause a check engine light or cruise control trouble.
issues.why: On some 1998 cars the wiring harness for the evaporative canister purge was routed in the wrong place at the factory.
issues.next: Check your VIN at nhtsa.gov or with a Cadillac dealer. The dealer reroutes and ties down the harness for free.

issues.t: Inner tie rod nuts can loosen (recall)
issues.sym: Loose or wandering steering, a clunk from the front when turning, or the car pulling unexpectedly.
issues.why: On a small group of 2000 Eldorados the inner tie rod nuts could loosen, and a tie rod could separate and cause sudden steering input.
issues.next: Check your VIN for recall 99V-301 at nhtsa.gov or with a Cadillac dealer. If your steering feels loose, stop driving and have it checked right away.

issues.t: Stalls or won't start from a failing crankshaft sensor
issues.sym: The engine shuts off while driving, cranks a long time before starting, or will not start at all. The check engine light may come on.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin saying the crankshaft position sensor on some 4.6L engines can fail. Owners describe stalling at speed and repeat sensor replacements.
issues.next: Have the codes read. A stall in traffic is a safety risk, so do not put this off. Use a quality sensor, since cheap ones are a common cause of repeat failures.

issues.t: Stumble or stall when coming to a stop
issues.sym: The engine stumbles, idles rough or dies as you slow down for a light or a stop.
issues.why: GM bulletin 150201 covers an intermittent stumble or stall when coming to a stop on these Northstar Cadillacs.
issues.next: Have a shop read the codes and check for engine computer updates and idle control problems. Stalling in traffic is a safety risk.

issues.t: Knock or tick noise on a cold start
issues.sym: A knocking or ticking noise from the engine for the first few seconds or minutes after a cold start that fades as it warms up.
issues.why: GM issued several bulletins on cold start knock and tick on the Northstar V8. It is often linked to piston slap or carbon and is sometimes paired with oil use.
issues.next: Note how long the noise lasts and whether oil use is rising. A noise that stays after warm-up or gets louder needs a proper diagnosis.

issues.t: Check engine light with chuggle or surge (torque converter clutch)
issues.sym: A shudder or surge at steady cruising speeds, often around 40-55 mph, with the check engine light on and code P0741.
issues.why: GM bulletins cover the torque converter clutch on the 4T80-E automatic slipping or not applying properly. One bulletin asks dealers to check the date code on the clutch control valve.
issues.next: Have the transmission codes read and check the fluid level and condition. Ask the shop about the GM bulletins before agreeing to a full rebuild.

issues.t: Buzz or moan when the torque converter locks up
issues.sym: A buzzing or moaning noise at cruising speed when the transmission locks up, usually in higher gears.
issues.why: GM bulletins for the 4T80-E automatic cover this noise and fix it by replacing a spacer plate and control valve parts.
issues.next: Mention the noise to a transmission shop and ask about the GM bulletin. It is not usually harmful, but have fluid checked.

issues.t: Speedometer drops out and cruise control quits
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on, the speedometer jumps around or stops, and cruise control and transmission lockup stop working.
issues.why: GM bulletins for these years cover this combination, which comes from a bad vehicle speed signal.
issues.next: Have the codes read and the speed sensor and wiring checked. Watch your speed carefully until it is fixed.

issues.t: Delayed or harsh shift into reverse or drive
issues.sym: A delay or hard clunk when shifting from Park into Reverse or Drive, or little engine braking in D3.
issues.why: GM bulletins from 1998 cover harsh or delayed engagement and missing engine braking on the 4T80-E automatic.
issues.next: Check the transmission fluid level and condition. Ask the shop about the bulletins and a fluid service before bigger repairs.

issues.t: ABS or traction light on or unwanted ABS activation
issues.sym: The ABS or traction control light comes on, a Traction message appears, or the ABS kicks in when it should not, sometimes with a noise from under the hood.
issues.why: GM bulletins cover codes C1225 and C1226 on these cars, which point to wheel speed sensor signals, the brake control module or low brake fluid.
issues.next: Have the ABS codes read. Normal brakes still work, but have it fixed promptly, especially if the ABS acts up in normal stops.

issues.t: Rusted or burst brake lines
issues.sym: The brake pedal sinks toward the floor, braking feels weak, or there is brake fluid under the car.
issues.why: Owners report steel brake lines rusting through and bursting on these older Eldorados, especially the rear lines in salt states.
issues.next: If the pedal goes soft, stop driving and have the car towed. Ask a shop to inspect all the brake lines, since more than one is often rusty.

issues.t: Brake pulsation and fast rotor wear
issues.sym: The steering wheel or pedal shakes when braking, or the brakes chatter, and rotors need replacing often.
issues.why: Owners report warped or worn front rotors and pulsation on these years, sometimes returning after brake work.
issues.next: Have the rotors measured and replaced with quality parts. Make sure the wheel lug nuts are tightened to spec with a torque wrench.

issues.t: Service StabiliTrak or check stability system message
issues.sym: A Service StabiliTrak or Check Stability System message, sometimes with traction control turning off.
issues.why: GM bulletins cover several StabiliTrak codes on these cars, and the steering wheel position sensor and wheel speed sensors are common causes.
issues.next: Have the stability system codes read. The brakes still work, but the car will not help you in a skid until it is fixed.

issues.t: Power steering shudder or moan when parking
issues.sym: A shudder, vibration or moaning noise through the steering wheel when turning slowly or parking.
issues.why: GM bulletins cover steering vibration and moan at low speed and general power steering concerns on 1998-2000 Cadillacs.
issues.next: Check the power steering fluid level and look for leaks. Ask a shop about the GM bulletins, which may call for a fluid flush or hose change.

issues.t: Front-end clunk or rattle over bumps
issues.sym: A clunk, rattle or metal-on-metal knock from the front of the car over bumps.
issues.why: GM bulletins cover front-end noise on these years. Worn stabilizer links and bushings are common causes.
issues.next: Have the front suspension checked. Links and bushings are low-cost parts.

issues.t: Trunk lid will not close or latch
issues.sym: The trunk lid will not pull down and lock, or it pops back up when you close it.
issues.why: The Eldorado trunk has a power pull-down feature. RepairPal lists a failed pull-down switch as a common problem.
issues.next: Have the pull-down motor and switch checked. Until it is fixed, tie the lid down so exhaust fumes cannot get in.

issues.t: Rear quarter trim panel sags or warps
issues.sym: The interior trim panels beside the rear seat sag, come loose or warp.
issues.why: GM released a repair kit for sagging and separating rear quarter trim panels on these cars.
issues.next: A body shop or dealer can fit the repair kit. It is a comfort issue, not a safety one.

issues.t: Door handles turn yellow on white cars
issues.sym: The painted outside door handles on white Eldorados turn yellow.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin on door handle discoloration on white-painted cars.
issues.next: This is cosmetic. Handles can be repainted or replaced if it bothers you.

issues.t: Heated front seat stops warming
issues.sym: One or both front seats stay cold when the seat heater is turned on.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin on front heated seats that are inoperative or cold.
issues.next: Have the seat heater switch, wiring and heating pad checked.

issues.t: Check engine light for a small evaporative leak
issues.sym: The check engine light comes on with code P0442, often after filling up.
issues.why: GM bulletin 3003 has technicians inspect the fuel filler neck for a small leak in the evaporative system.
issues.next: Make sure the gas cap is tight and in good shape. If the light comes back, have the filler neck and evap system smoke-tested.

issues.t: Fuel gauge swings when the tank is full
issues.sym: The fuel gauge jumps between full and empty right after filling up.
issues.why: GM bulletins for 1998 cover a fuel gauge that fluctuates when the tank is full.
issues.next: Note how the gauge acts as the tank drops. Use the trip meter to track fuel until the sending unit is checked.

issues.t: Power door locks stop working
issues.sym: The power door locks do not respond to the switch or remote.
issues.why: GM issued a bulletin for inoperative power door locks on the 1996 Eldorado.
issues.next: Have a shop check the lock switch, relay and door actuators.

issues.t: Snap or click from the steering column when turning
issues.sym: A snap or click felt and heard in the steering column when turning the wheel.
issues.why: GM bulletin 97-09-01-32-02B covers a snap or click noise from the steering column on these cars.
issues.next: Have the steering column checked and ask the shop about the bulletin.
